advances: For every spatial field on the unchanged height-lifted tree, entropy outside its exactly \(mQ\) largest scalar coordinate contributions either directly supplies the required original cubic-depth-moment scale, or leaves a set of at most \(64(Q+1)^{11}\) strong coordinates with path variation at most one on its complement. The spatial fourth-ratio estimate holds on every level without a depth-homogeneity assumption. This is an arithmetic reduction; no geometric forest theorem or general all-support moment inequality is asserted or used.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The exact source/path construction and level parametrization are from 032423921efad6c8; the full original height columns and their parameter specialization are from 604889294a17d7df; the scalar function and its evenness, monotonicity, and small-argument lower bound are those of d63d54549cda4df4, with their elementary derivation included above. All adaptive transcript, full-normalizer, entrance-atom, strong-coordinate-count, and path-variation arguments are proved here.
proof:
Since \(b_8=\lfloor2^8/(8\cdot8)\rfloor=4\), we have \(Q\ge4\). In particular \(m,Q\) are positive, \(a_s\le k\) for all \(s\), and all original height columns are nonempty. Also \(m^r\ge m\) for \(1\le r\le Q\), so \(n=\sum_{r=1}^{Q}m^r\ge mQ\). This verifies the exact cardinality required of \(T_0\).

We recall the scalar properties with their normalization checked. As proved for \(\mathcal R\) in d63d54549cda4df4, direct algebra, with \(v=(e^x-1)/(e^x+1)\), gives \(R(x)=1+6v^2+v^4\). Hence \(R(x)\ge1\), \(\log R(x)\ge0\), and \(R\) is even and nondecreasing in \(|x|\): for \(x\ge0\), \(v\ge0\) and \(v'=2e^x/(e^x+1)^2>0\). For completeness, when \(0\le x\le\log2\), one has \(x/3\le v\le1/3\), since \(e^x-1\ge x\) and \(e^x+1\le3\). Thus \(R(x)-1\ge2x^2/3\) and \(R(x)\le136/81<2\). The integral inequality \(\log y=\int_1^y dt/t\ge(y-1)/y\) for \(y\ge1\) gives
$$
\log R(x)\ge\frac{R(x)-1}{R(x)}\ge\frac{x^2}{3}
\qquad(0\le x\le\log2).
$$
These are exactly the scalar properties we use from d63d54549cda4df4, with \(R=\mathcal R\). Moreover \(\varepsilon=1/(mQ)\le1/8<\log2\), since \(\log2=\int_1^2dt/t\ge1/2\). They apply at \(\varepsilon\) without any restriction on other field magnitudes.

Fix \(s\in\lbrace0,\ldots,Q\rbrace\). An ordered transcript \(\vartheta=(c_1,\ldots,c_s)\in D_m^s\) recursively defines nodes \(u_0=\varnothing\) and \(u_r=u_{r-1}i_m(c_r)\), together with the source assignments \(b[u_{r-1}]=c_r\) for \(1\le r\le s\). Write \(\mathcal V_\vartheta\) for the union of these child-coordinate blocks, and \(c_{\vartheta,u}\) for the assigned Boolean value at \(u\in\mathcal V_\vartheta\). The blocks are disjoint: their coordinates have distinct depths for different \(r\). Thus \(|\mathcal V_\vartheta|=ms\), regardless of the adaptive locations selected by the transcript. No condition is imposed on any coordinate outside \(\mathcal V_\vartheta\).

Every extension of these assignments is a Boolean source whose first \(s\) path steps are the specified ones, by induction on the path construction of 032423921efad6c8. Conversely, every Boolean source with \(h(b)\ge s\) gives one such transcript. Reducing \(z_s(b)\) modulo two recovers \(b\), so the source-to-level-point map is injective. Therefore the resulting transcript classes are a disjoint partition of \(\mathcal L_s\). This is precisely the adaptive-source parametrization underlying the level census in 032423921efad6c8, here retaining the field weights on every free coordinate.

For a transcript define the positive fixed factor
$$
C_\vartheta(\gamma)
=\exp\left(
\sum_{u\in\mathcal V_\vartheta}\gamma_u c_{\vartheta,u}
+2\sum_{r=1}^{s}\gamma_{u_r}\right).
$$
All selected nodes \(u_r\) lie in \(\mathcal V_\vartheta\), so this includes every source-dependent spike factor. The contribution of this transcript to \(Z_s(\gamma)\) is exactly
$$
Y_\vartheta(\gamma)
=C_\vartheta(\gamma)
\prod_{u\notin\mathcal V_\vartheta}(1+e^{\gamma_u}).
$$
Indeed, the remaining source entries are unrestricted independent Boolean choices in the finite sum, and the selected spike positions are fixed by the transcript. The free-coordinate set may vary with \(\vartheta\); no equality of these products is assumed. The fixed factor obeys \(C_\vartheta(4\gamma)=C_\vartheta(\gamma)^4\), for every real field. Consequently it cancels in the fourth ratio, giving
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Y_\vartheta(4\gamma)}{Y_\vartheta(\gamma)^4}
&=\prod_{u\notin\mathcal V_\vartheta}
\frac{1+e^{4\gamma_u}}{(1+e^{\gamma_u})^4}\\
&=8^{-(n-ms)}
\exp\left(\sum_{u\notin\mathcal V_\vartheta}\beta_u\right)
\ge8^{-(n-ms)}\exp(E_{\mathrm{rem}}).
\end{aligned}
$$
To justify the final inequality uniformly over the varying free-coordinate sets, all \(\beta_u\) are nonnegative and \(|\mathcal V_\vartheta|=ms\le mQ=|T_0|\). The definition of the largest \(mQ\) values implies \(\sum_{u\in\mathcal V_\vartheta}\beta_u\le\sum_{u\in T_0}\beta_u\), by first extending \(\mathcal V_\vartheta\) to \(mQ\) coordinates if necessary. Subtracting from the total entropy proves the required lower bound on each free sum separately.

There are exactly \(J_s=|D_m|^s\) transcripts, where \(1\le J_s\le2^{ms}\). Indeed, the symmetric saturated chain containing the empty Boolean set also contains \([m]\), and hence has a nonterminal vertex because \(m\ge1\). Applying the finite fourth-power inequality \((\sum_{j=1}^{J_s} y_j)^4\le J_s^3\sum_{j=1}^{J_s}y_j^4\) to the positive values \(Y_\vartheta(\gamma)\), and summing the preceding ratio bounds, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_s(4\gamma)
&\ge8^{-(n-ms)}e^{E_{\mathrm{rem}}}
\sum_{\vartheta\in D_m^s}Y_\vartheta(\gamma)^4\\
&\ge8^{-(n-ms)}e^{E_{\mathrm{rem}}}J_s^{-3}Z_s(\gamma)^4
\ge8^{-n}e^{E_{\mathrm{rem}}}Z_s(\gamma)^4.
\end{aligned}
$$
For clarity, the finite fourth-power inequality follows by applying Cauchy-Schwarz twice: \((\sum y_j)^2\le J_s\sum y_j^2\) and \((\sum y_j^2)^2\le J_s\sum y_j^4\). The last displayed inequality uses \(J_s^3\le2^{3ms}=8^{ms}\). At \(s=0\) there is one empty transcript, \(\mathcal V_\vartheta\) is empty, and all \(n\) coordinates are free, so the same proof applies. At \(s=Q\) only the first \(Q\) visited blocks are fixed, with no stopping condition beyond reaching depth \(Q\); exactly \(mQ\) coordinates are fixed and the same proof again applies. This proves the spatial estimate at every level, including both endpoints.

We next retain the exact original height normalization from 604889294a17d7df. Define the finite height tails \(L_s^{\mathrm{ht}}=\sum_{t=a_s}^{k}2^{-t}\) and full level masses \(W_s=L_s^{\mathrm{ht}}Z_s(\gamma)\). They satisfy \(W=\sum_{s=0}^{Q}W_s\), where \(W\) includes all columns and every original allowed height. Each \(W_s\) is positive, and some \(s_*\in\lbrace0,\ldots,Q\rbrace\) has \(W_{s_*}\ge W/(Q+1)\). Exact geometric summation, including when \(a_s=k\), gives
$$
L_s^{\mathrm{ht}}
=2^{1-a_s}\left(1-2^{-(k-a_s+1)}\right),
\qquad 2^{-a_s}\le L_s^{\mathrm{ht}}\le2^{1-a_s}.
$$
Every \((z,a_{s_*})\), \(z\in\mathcal L_{s_*}\), is an original entrance atom. Keeping precisely these atoms in the fourth-power sum and using the spatial estimate yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}^4
&\ge\frac{2^{-4a_{s_*}}Z_{s_*}(4\gamma)}{W^4}\\
&=\left(\frac{W_{s_*}}W\right)^4
\left(\frac{2^{-a_{s_*}}}{L_{s_*}^{\mathrm{ht}}}\right)^4
\frac{Z_{s_*}(4\gamma)}{Z_{s_*}(\gamma)^4}\\
&\ge\frac{8^{-n}e^{E_{\mathrm{rem}}}}{16(Q+1)^4}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Since \(N=n+1\) and \(m=2(Q+1)^4\), multiplication by \(8^N\) gives exactly \(8^N\sum p_{\mathbf I}^4\ge e^{E_{\mathrm{rem}}}/m\). No level restriction or discarded atom has been used to redefine \(W\) or \(p\). Every closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf I\) contains its atom of probability \(p_{\mathbf I}\); hence \(\tau_p(\mathbf I)\ge p_{\mathbf I}\) and \(M_3(p)\ge\sum p_{\mathbf I}^4\). If \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge\log m\), these inequalities prove \(M_3(p)\ge8^{-N}\).

Finally suppose \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}<\log m\), and set \(J=\lbrace u\notin T_0:|\gamma_u|>\varepsilon\rbrace\). By scalar evenness and monotonicity, every \(u\in J\) satisfies \(\beta_u\ge\log R(\varepsilon)\ge\varepsilon^2/3\). All other terms in \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}\) are nonnegative. Thus
$$
|J|\frac{\varepsilon^2}{3}
\le\sum_{u\in J}\beta_u
\le E_{\mathrm{rem}},
\qquad
|T|=|T_0|+|J|
\le mQ+3m^2Q^2E_{\mathrm{rem}}
<mQ+3m^2Q^2\log m.
$$
This also covers \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}=0\), when the inequality forces \(J\) to be empty. To verify the numerical polynomial bound without an asymptotic estimate, use \(\log2<1\) and \(\log(Q+1)\le Q\) to obtain \(\log m=\log2+4\log(Q+1)\le5(Q+1)\). Hence
$$
\begin{aligned}
mQ+3m^2Q^2\log m
&\le2Q(Q+1)^4+60Q^2(Q+1)^9\\
&\le2(Q+1)^5+60(Q+1)^{11}
\le62(Q+1)^{11}
\le64(Q+1)^{11}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The definition of \(T=T_0\cup J\) gives \(|\gamma_u|\le\varepsilon\) outside \(T\). Any full rooted path has \(Q\) disjoint child blocks of size \(m\), so its sum of absolute values for the field \(\gamma\mathbf1_{\mathcal T_{m,Q}\setminus T}\) is at most \(mQ\varepsilon=1\). Taking the maximum over those paths proves \(\Pi(\gamma\mathbf1_{\mathcal T_{m,Q}\setminus T})\le1\), completing the dichotomy.
statement:
Fix an integer \(k\ge8\). Use the specialization \(\rho_t=2^{-t}\) of 604889294a17d7df and the exact tree construction of 032423921efad6c8. Explicitly, put \(b_\ell=0\) for \(1\le\ell<8\), \(b_\ell=\lfloor2^\ell/(8\ell)\rfloor\) for \(8\le\ell\le k\), \(Q_0=0\), \(Q_\ell=\sum_{r=1}^{\ell}b_r\), \(Q=Q_k\), \(m=2(Q+1)^4\), \(n=n_{m,Q}=\sum_{r=1}^{Q}m^r\), and \(N=n+1\). Here \(k\) is the height cutoff, \(Q\) is the tree depth, and \(n\) is the spatial dimension. Let \(a_0=0\) and \(a_s=\ell\) whenever \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\).

Coordinates are indexed by \(\mathcal T_{m,Q}=\bigcup_{r=1}^{Q}[m]^r\). For every node \(v\) of depth less than \(Q\), its child block has coordinates \(v1,\ldots,vm\), with the empty word as root. Choose any symmetric saturated chain partition of \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace^m\), and retain its nonterminal set \(D_m\) and successor \(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\) from 032423921efad6c8. For a Boolean source \(b\), its forward path starts at the root and selects child \(v i_m(b[v])\) whenever \(b[v]\in D_m\), stopping otherwise or at depth \(Q\); write its length as \(h(b)\). The level-\(s\) point is \(z_s(b)=b+2\sum_{r=1}^{s}e_{u_r}\) for \(s\le h(b)\), where \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h(b)}\) is this path. Let \(A_{m,Q}\) be the union of these points, and write \(\mathcal L_s=\lbrace z\in A_{m,Q}:\operatorname{level}(z)=s\rbrace\). Thus all recurring supports and path objects have the original normalization of 032423921efad6c8. The full original height support is
$$
\widehat A
=\lbrace(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\quad a_{\operatorname{level}(z)}\le t\le k,\quad t\in\mathbb Z\rbrace.
$$

For every real spatial field \(\gamma=(\gamma_u)_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}}\), define \(Z_s(\gamma)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal L_s}\exp(\sum_u\gamma_u z_u)\) for \(0\le s\le Q\), and put
$$
R(x)=\frac{8(1+e^{4x})}{(1+e^x)^4},\qquad
\beta_u=\log R(\gamma_u),\qquad
\varepsilon=\frac1{mQ}.
$$
The scalar \(R\) is exactly \(\mathcal R\) in d63d54549cda4df4. Choose any set \(T_0\subseteq\mathcal T_{m,Q}\) of exactly \(mQ\) coordinates having the largest values of \(\beta_u\), with arbitrary tie breaking, and put \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}=\sum_{u\notin T_0}\beta_u\). Such a set exists because \(n\ge mQ\). Then, simultaneously for every \(0\le s\le Q\),
$$
\frac{Z_s(4\gamma)}{Z_s(\gamma)^4}
\ge 8^{-n}\exp(E_{\mathrm{rem}}).
$$

On \(\widehat A\) use every original height atom with weight \(w_{(z,t)}=\exp(\sum_u\gamma_u z_u)2^{-t}\), with zero weight off \(\widehat A\), full normalizer \(W=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}w_{\mathbf I}\), and \(p_{\mathbf I}=w_{\mathbf I}/W\). Define the actual discrete depth in the original ambient space by \(\tau_p(\mathbf I)=\inf\lbrace p(H):H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }\mathbf I\rbrace\), and \(M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}\tau_p(\mathbf I)^3\). Then
$$
8^N\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}^4
\ge \frac{\exp(E_{\mathrm{rem}})}m,
\qquad
M_3(p)\ge\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}^4.
$$
Consequently, if \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge\log m\), the unchanged original law satisfies \(M_3(p)\ge8^{-N}\).

If instead \(E_{\mathrm{rem}}<\log m\), the explicit set
$$
T=T_0\cup\lbrace u\notin T_0:|\gamma_u|>\varepsilon\rbrace
$$
satisfies \(T\supseteq T_0\), \(|\gamma_u|\le\varepsilon\) outside \(T\), and
$$
|T|\le mQ+3m^2Q^2 E_{\mathrm{rem}}
<mQ+3m^2Q^2\log m
\le64(Q+1)^{11}.
$$
For a field \(\theta\) on the tree, let
$$
\Pi(\theta)
=\max_{\substack{u_0=\varnothing,\ u_r\in[m]^r\\
u_r\text{ is a child of }u_{r-1}\ (1\le r\le Q)}}
\sum_{r=0}^{Q-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|\theta_{u_r i}|.
$$
Thus \(\Pi\) sums absolute field over the child blocks along one full rooted path, rather than just the selected path coordinates. The small-entropy alternative gives \(\Pi(\gamma\mathbf1_{\mathcal T_{m,Q}\setminus T})\le1\). These conclusions hold for arbitrary signs and magnitudes of \(\gamma_u\) and every allowed chain partition. The notation \(M_3(p)\) denotes this depth moment and does not change the maximum-atom meaning of \(M(w)\) in 604889294a17d7df.
